newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish banks see cost of euro at FIM 600-700 mln.
newsitem.headline: Finnish banks see cost of euro at FIM 600-700 mln.

text.p: Finnish banks expect direct costs of adapting the banking system to a single currency to be in the region of 600 million to 700 million markka, the Bankers' Association said on Monday.
Its previous cost estimate was about one billion markka.

"The costs for Finnish banks of introducing the euro seem to be lower than earlier estimates, in total 600-700 million markka, of which about half is information technology costs," the association said in a statement.
The fact that the Finnish banking system is already highly developed and automated reduces costs, it said.
"Apart from information technology costs, e.g. money handling and equipment costs, personnel training and information will bring notable costs for banks," it said.
Merita, the cooperative banking group, state-owned Postipankki and the savings banks contributed to the estimate, the association said.

Merita said in a separate statement that its direct costs from introducing the euro would be 200 million markka -- 120 million in information systems -- and Postipankki said its costs would rise to a maximum of 150 million markka.
The European bankers' federation has estimated in 1994-1995 that for the entire EU, introducing the euro would cost some 50 billion markka, the association said.
"There have been signals from elsewhere in Europe that previous estimates are proving too small," it said.
